## 席位核对

**REWORK** — head `def2f649`. L1 per `references/l1-review-checklist.md` (origin/main). CI green on this head (48 success, 17 skipped; the Check Changeset `cancelled` row is superseded by a success on the same head, not a red). Two correctness defects in the save path, and the card's live acceptance is not yet met.

### 1. The menu save writes the *served* navigation, so translations get baked into the stored app

- `DesignModeMenu.tsx` (≈160–169) seeds the editor from the sidebar's `activeApp.navigation`, i.e. the served document, and `commit` hands the whole `navigation` to `saveAppMenu`.
- `designModeMenuSave.ts` `saveAppMenu` then writes `{ ...served, name, navigation }` into the app (or its `.custom` pair).
- The served navigation has gone through `translateApp` (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` ≈2180), which replaces each node's `label` with `apps.<app>.navigation.<id>.label` for the session's locale.
- Consequence: a zh-CN admin who adds one entry stores **Chinese labels on every existing entry**. Those slots now diverge from the packaged base, so under ADR-0029 D9.2a the deployment catalog no longer applies to them, and an English reader sees Chinese from then on. Studio's nav save (`StudioDesignSurface`, ≈3700–3765) avoids this by saving its stored `appDraft`.

### 2. The served navigation is pruned per caller, so a whole-tree save can drop entries

- `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:1105` `filterNav` removes entries the caller may not open before the document is served.
- Saving that tree whole stores the pruned tree: entries the editing admin cannot open (another app's object, a permission-gated page) are silently removed for everyone.

**Fix asked for (1 and 2):** compose the save from the **stored** navigation (`client.get` of the stored document, not the served one), applying the staged edits (add / move / rename / remove) by entry id; leave untouched entries byte-identical. Pin two cases: a translated-label case (served label differs from stored → stored label survives the save) and a pruned-entry case (an entry absent from the served tree survives the save).

### 3. Live acceptance owed

The PR records the live run in English on the showcase only ("HotCRM itself was not run here"). The card's acceptance is HotCRM in zh-CN: one add and one move, saved. Please run that once on the fixed head and show, from the network: the stored body's labels (untranslated, unchanged for entries you did not touch), an English reader's menu unchanged apart from the edit, and a member seeing the change.

### 4. Question for the seat (not a ruling)

A rename made in a non-source language is stored as a plain string on `label`, not as a locale entry, so it becomes every language's label. If that is the intended behaviour, say so in the PR body; if not, it is a card, not part of this rework.

Re-request L1 on the new head; the review will be a delta on items 1–3.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `def2f649cf8c9a378603d9c813452433b12c3cdb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #36363 (body and all five comments, including the added leave-prompt requirement 7079728193 and the entry move 7080271489), PR #36437 (body, 24-file list, net diff against main), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at `def2f649` only to judge the diff.

Gates: every completed check-run on the head is success or skipped. Test UI 12/16 went red on its first attempt on the known main flake #36500 (plugin-form, a file this PR does not touch) and its second attempt is success. One Check Changeset run is cancelled as a superseded duplicate; two other Check Changeset runs on the head are success. Test Core and Build Core are skipped because the diff touches no core path, which is right for a `ui/`-only diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set. The diff adds the design-mode menu editor (`DesignModeMenu.tsx`), its pure tree edits (`designModeMenu.ts`) and its write (`designModeMenuSave.ts`); swaps the sidebar's plain menu for the editor only when the mode is on, in the sidebar, in an app, with no areas (`UnifiedSidebar.tsx`); and lets a read-only package's 「Edit app」 enter the mode (`ShellPageActions.tsx`). Right: every visible change is gated on `designMode`, and the outside-the-mode test in `UnifiedSidebar.favoritesMenu-12427.test.tsx` pins that no 「Add menu item」 and no editor 「⋮」 appear otherwise (card acceptance item 8).
- Where the edits are saved. Right. `saveAppMenu` writes the app document with its new `navigation` into the app's own package when the server lists it writable, else into the paired customization package from the ensure door, with `overrideDraftBody` declaring the override at the base's listed version. That is the customization layer Studio's nav save writes (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` around line 3730), never the installed package's source. `designModeMenuSave-36363.test.ts` pins both targets and the override declaration.
- Who may save. Right. Entering the mode is gated by `useAppStudioEntry` / `useStudioEntryGate` (a workspace administrator holding `manage_metadata`, on a listed, non-kernel package). The new read-only branch adds the wall check `!postureHasOrgWall(posture) || user.isPlatformAdmin`, which matches the server's ensure door (`packages-ensure-customization.test.ts`: under `isolated` and `group` a tenant administrator is refused 403 and the operator admitted; under `single` a `manage_metadata` holder is admitted). The server's write gate stays the authority. `ShellPageActions-36111.test.tsx` pins the read-only entry, the walled eye, and the writable package under the wall.
- Refusal and undo on a bad save. Right. The draft is written with `ifNoneMatch: '*'`, so a pending Studio draft is refused with the localised `pendingDraft` sentence and nothing is published; a refused publish resets the draft this save wrote and passes the refusal on. The mode's own rule (#36362) keeps the failed change staged and the mode on. 「Cancel」 drops everything, and nothing staged was written. The tests pin the pending-draft refusal, the publish-refused discard, and Cancel after three edits writing nothing.
- Editor and runtime sidebar read the same order. Right. The editor reads `activeApp.navigation` and gives ids only to entries without one, without reordering. The sidebar reads the same `activeApp.navigation` through `withoutUnreadableObjectEntries` and `applyPins`, and both filter or flag entries without reordering them. A landed publish calls `emitMetadataRefresh`, so the app and its menu are read again.
- Leave prompt (comment 7079728193). Right as the comment allows. The menu stages through the mode, which registers the shell's one unsaved-edits prompt. The comment says to use the shell's prompt where one exists, so its two choices (stay, leave) are acceptable in place of the three the coordinator suggested. Three component tests pin it: the app switch asks, staying keeps the move, and a reload or close is held only while the change is unsaved.
- Picker offers only what is not in the menu (card item 2). Partly wrong. See S1.
- Tests against the card's acceptance list. Add, move up, move to group, remove and offer again, rename, cancel, outside the mode, and the leave prompt each have a component test. Drag is pinned only through the pure `moveEntry` placement tests; the `onDragEnd` wiring has none (N4). Cross-account visibility and HotCRM are live checks for the coordinator after merge, as the card's comment 7079728193 says.
- Public surface. No new export from `@object-ui/app-shell` (the editor is a lazy default import inside the package). New `@object-ui/i18n` keys under `designMode.menu`: 36 lines in each of the eleven locales, with the de quote-pair and ellipsis pins recounted.

S1 (should-fix): The picker's "already in the menu" test misses views that the menu names in the short form. `targetKeyOf` turns an object entry with `viewName: 'my_projects'` into `view/my_projects`, while the picker keys its rows by the listed view's name, which is always the qualified `object.key` (`ViewItemNameSchema`), for example `view/crm_project.my_projects`. The two never match, so any view the app's menu names in the short form is offered again as "not in the menu", and picking it adds a duplicate entry. The short form is the authored form in practice: HotCRM's `psa.app.ts` and `crm.app.ts` "My Work" entries, `examples/app-todo`, and the spec's own example. Every test uses only the qualified form (`designModeMenu-36363.test.ts`, `crm_opportunity.mine`), so nothing catches it. Fix: in `targetKeyOf`, qualify a `viewName` that has no dot with the entry's `objectName` (the same normalisation `ObjectView` applies to a requested view), and add a test with a short-form `viewName`.

N1 (nit): `saveAppMenu` asks the ensure door, which creates the customization package on first use, before it checks for the base version, so the `noVersion` refusal can come after a package write. The dashboard path (`resolveDashboardEditTarget` / `ensureDashboardSaveTarget` in `runtime-metadata-persistence.ts`) checks the version first and also refuses an ensured pair that is not `writable`; this save does neither. The test "refused before anything is written" only rules out `save` calls, not `ensure`. In practice the server's ensure door refuses a base with no SemVer version itself, so the effect is small.

N2 (nit): The `designMode.tsx` docblock still says who may enter is "a workspace administrator holding `manage_metadata` on a writable package". After this PR a read-only package's app enters too, so that sentence no longer holds. Separately, while the tenancy posture is still being read, `postureHasOrgWall(undefined)` is false, so a walled deployment can briefly show 「Edit app」 to a tenant administrator. The server still refuses the save with 403.

N3 (nit): Studio's nav save sends `navPayloadOf(editorNav)`, which leaves out entries that name no target for their type. The design-mode save writes the served `navigation` unfiltered, so an app whose served menu holds such an entry could be refused here where Studio's save is accepted.

N4 (nit): Card acceptance item 3 (drag an entry to another group and save) has no component test of the `onDragEnd` wiring. Only the pure placement function underneath it is pinned.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/36363-design-mode-menu-editing.md` takes `patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`. Both lines are present and line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. The diff adds new published `@object-ui/i18n` keys and a new console capability, and removes or narrows nothing a consumer reads. The read-only posture now shows 「Edit app」 instead of the eye for a customization-capable caller, which widens what such a caller can do.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The save writes only keys the spec already accepts (`navigation` entries of the existing `object`, `dashboard`, `report`, `page` and `url` types, `label`, `icon`, `id`, and `overrides` from the existing customization body). It adds no authorable key, accepted value or metadata type.
- Level. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3, a non-protocol change ships `patch`, widening included. `patch` on both moved packages is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- ADR-0146 D5 (a read-only package's app shows the eye into Studio). The PR changes this for a caller the customization door admits, because card item 7 asks for it. Item 7 is in the card's "要做的" list and not among the items the coordinator says it added. The PR says the seat recorded the D5 row on ADR revision card #36086. That card is outside this review's inputs, so the record could not be checked here. The diff touches no ADR file, so no governed surface is hit. Answered by the card; the D5 row is left to #36086.
- Entry moved to the app-name menu (#36485, comment 7080271489). The comment says whichever of the two cards merges second makes the installed-app path work through the new entry. This PR lands first and keeps the change to one condition on the existing button. Answered.
- Leave prompt with three choices (comment 7079728193). The shell's two-choice prompt is used, as the comment allows. Answered.
- An app whose menu is split into areas is drawn unedited in the mode. The card edits `navigation`, and the PR says neither the showcase nor HotCRM has such an app. Declared, and acceptable for this stage.
- The card's "没有核对的" items. Whether the runtime can call Studio's save is answered: it writes the same document through the same doors. Whether an installed app's customization survives a package upgrade is not measured by this PR. It is the ADR-0146 D3 override mechanism Studio already uses, and stays the coordinator's live check. Whether a view menu entry is the same kind of thing as a favorited view is not addressed. The editor leaves personal favorites alone, as the card's out-of-scope list says.
- `open_questions`: the PR declares none beyond the above.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5). Not applicable. The diff adds no data query, no id materialisation and no in-app join over records. The picker's lists are metadata-registry reads (`client.list` per kind and per package, at most ten, run one after another), and the "not in the menu" filter is a set difference over the menu tree, which no SQL query could do.
- Out of scope: #36366, the card's later stage, was not reviewed.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** (delta L1 since REWORK 7081226692) at head `11b0e584`.
- l1-face is CLEAN: 47 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- The delta is `aed9f080` (the save-path rework and ruling (4)) and `11b0e584` (a test-typing fix for TS7053).

### Items 1 and 2: the save writes the stored menu, not the translated or pruned served one. Closed.

- `saveAppMenu` now reads the stored app through the layered read, `layered('app', name, { packageId })`, taking `effective ?? code`. It no longer uses `client.get`.
- It replays the editor's edits on the stored navigation with `rebaseMenuEdits(served, navigation, stored)`, then passes the result through `navPayloadOf`, as Studio's nav save does.
- The patch is computed per entry id from served-before against edited. A label the reader did not touch therefore produces no patch, and the stored value, language map or source string, stays as it is.
- Removed entries are dropped. Added and moved entries are placed after their nearest edited predecessor. Order is kept by a longest-common-subsequence run per group, so a neighbour's removal does not count as a move.
- Every other stored entry is written back as the same object. That includes entries `filterNav` pruned from the reader. An id-less stored entry is matched to its served copy's assigned id by group, type and target.
- Pins added in `designModeMenuSave-36363`: a zh-CN move writes the stored English labels; a pruned entry stays where it was stored; a rename writes only the key it changed; id-less entries are matched and written without an id; an entry with no target is left out.
- The order is also right now: `overrideDraftBody` and its version check run before `ensureCustomization`, and a pair that comes back not writable is refused before anything is written.

### Item 3: the live run on HotCRM in zh-CN. Closed.

The run used HotCRM 6.5.0 on a fresh database, with this branch's console, signed in as admin. `/i18n/locales` marks `en` as the default.
- The edits were one move (客户 above 线索) and one add (活动参与者 under 数据洞察). The network shows the layered read, then `ensure-customization`, then `PUT …?mode=draft&package=…hotcrm.custom`, then `publish`.
- In the PUT body, `navigation` contains no CJK character. It holds the 34 stored entries plus the 1 added. None of the 8 contributed entries is written, and no untouched entry's own keys differ from what is stored.
- With the two edits undone, the stored menu after the save equals the stored menu before, byte for byte. The same holds for the menu served to an English reader.
- A member, in both en and zh-CN, sees the moved order and the added entry. The files are in `repo-objectstack-7/shots/36363/`, along with `hotcrm-network.json`.

### Item 4: ruling (4) as the seat gave it. Read.

- Rename is open only when the session language is the deployment default (`isSameLanguage`; `en` matches `en-US`, `zh-CN` does not match `zh-TW`) and the entry's shown label equals its stored label. Otherwise the name field is disabled with the source-language hint, and the icon alone is saved. This is pinned under zh-CN.
- Adding, moving and the icon stay open in every language.
- The body names the limits: no server `sourceLocale` yet, and no console path for writing a translation. #36504 carries both.

### Also read

- **Contributed entries.** Entries from another package's `navigationContributions` are not in the stored menu. Their move, rename and remove are disabled with a hint. Without that, a moved contributed entry would be written into the menu and served twice. This is in-surface, found live, and pinned.
- **View keys.** `targetKeyOf` now qualifies a bare `viewName` with its object, matching HotCRM's `viewName: 'my_projects'` form.
- **Changeset.** The added sentences, read one by one against the diff, are all true: composed from the stored app, replayed by entry id, untouched entries written as they were, rename in the default language only, add, move and icon open in every language, contributed entries not editable here.
- **The scripts/ gate red.** The only red in `vitest run scripts/` is `date-only-zone-pins-10183`, a TZ order dependence this PR does not touch. #36492 carries it, and it does not block this PR.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `11b0e584c5201c457664774fcc248576eab75c2f`
Local-runs: probe — one node run of the pure `rebaseMenuEdits` (the head's `designModeMenu.ts`, copied to scratch, no build and no test suite) on four small menus, to confirm M1 and S2 before a FAIL was written on them

Delta review of the record at `def2f649` (comment 7081253549). Inputs read: card #36363 (body and all five comments), PR #36437 (body, both comments: the L1 REWORK 7081226692 and the earlier record, the 25-file list, the net diff against main), the two new commits `aed9f08072a` and `11b0e584c52`, and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head only to judge the diff. The seat ruling (4) on renames is not written on the card or the PR; it was read from the PR body and from follow-up card #36504, which state it the same way.

Gates: every check-run on the head is success or skipped. Type Check UI is success, all 16 Test UI shards are success, both Check Changeset runs are success. Test Core shards and Build Core are skipped, which is right for a `ui/`-only diff. The #36492 red the PR body names is a local run of `vitest run scripts/`; no check-run on the head is red.

### ① Derived judgments

- Save path, the normal case. Right. `saveAppMenu` no longer writes the served menu. It reads the app as stored (`client.layered`, `effective ?? code`), replays the edits on the stored navigation by entry id (`rebaseMenuEdits`), and writes `{ ...stored, name, navigation }`. The server's layered view serves a caller who may write the app its stored version, unpruned (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`, the `author-exempt` rule). An untouched entry is the same object, a patch writes only the keys that changed, and a stored entry the reader was never shown stays in place. Pinned in `designModeMenuSave-36363.test.ts`: the translated-label case and the pruned-entry case the L1 rework asked for, the one-key rename, and id-less stored entries.
- Save path, another package's entries. Wrong. See M1. The save can still write a served, localized entry into the stored menu.
- The stored menu changed under the editor. Mostly right. The stored menu is read at save time, so the edits land on the newest stored version and another administrator's published changes are kept. A draft left pending is refused by the first-write pin. Two gaps: an entry the editor moved that has since left the stored menu is written back from its served copy (M1, same line of code), and nothing pins the stored version between the read and the draft write (N6).
- Rename rule, as ruled. Right. `nameOpen` opens the name field only when the session language is the deployment's default (`GET /api/v1/i18n/locales`, `isDefault`, `en` matching `en-US`) and the entry's shown label equals its stored label. Otherwise the field is disabled with the hint, and `onDone` writes the icon alone. It fails closed: while the default language or the stored menu is still being read, or when either read fails, the field is disabled. Adding, moving and the icon stay open in every language. Pinned by the zh-CN case, the differing-label case in the default language, and `isSameLanguage`. The translation write path is #36504, not this PR.
- Who may enter the mode and save. Right, and unchanged since `def2f649`. `ShellPageActions.tsx` and `UnifiedSidebar.tsx` did not change in the two new commits. Entry is still `useAppStudioEntry` plus, for a read-only package, `!postureHasOrgWall(posture) || user.isPlatformAdmin`. The new stored read goes through the server's own read gate, and the write still goes through the server's write and ensure doors. No permission is widened.
- Check order before the write. Right. The base's version is read before the ensure door is asked, and a pair answered not writable is refused before anything is written to it. Both are pinned.
- Public surface. No new export from the `@object-ui/app-shell` package index. `@object-ui/i18n` gains three more keys under `designMode.menu` in each of the eleven locales (the rename hint, the contributed-entry sentence, the not-writable refusal).

Earlier findings, by id:

S1: closed. `targetKeyOf` now qualifies a `viewName` without a dot with the entry's `objectName`, and `designModeMenu-36363.test.ts` pins the short form.

N1: closed. `overrideDraftBody` and the version check run before `ensureCustomization`, a pair that is not writable is refused, and a test pins that the only call before the refusal is the layered read.

N2: open in part. The `designMode.tsx` docblock now says a read-only package's app enters too. The other half stands: while the tenancy posture is still being read, a walled deployment can briefly show 「Edit app」 to a tenant administrator. The server still refuses the save.

N3: closed. The save sends `navPayloadOf(...)`, as Studio's nav save does, and a test pins that an entry naming no target is left out.

N4: closed. A component test now drives `DndContext`'s `onDragEnd` for a drop on another group's end and a drop on an entry elsewhere, and checks the saved result.

New findings:

M1 (must-fix): One 「Move down」 writes another package's entry into the app's stored menu. Contributed entries are appended at the end of their group or of the top level (`registry-apps.ts` `applyNavContributions`), so the last own entry of such a group has 「Move down」 enabled (`canMoveBy` does not look at `fixed`). Pressing it swaps the entry with the first contributed one. In `rebaseMenuEdits`, `staysInOrder` breaks the tie of a swap by treating the later entry in the served order as the moved one, which here is the contributed entry. It is not in the stored menu, so `taken.get(id)` is empty and the line `const entry = taken.get(id) ?? now.entry` writes its served copy. Probe result for stored `[lead, account]`, served `[lead, account, quote(contributed, label 报价)]`, after one 「Move down」 on `account`: the menu written is `[lead, quote{label: 报价}, account]`. The contributed entry is now stored, with the reader's localized label, and it is served twice from then on, because the contribution is appended again with no de-duplication. That is the harm the PR body and the changeset say cannot happen ("it is not moved, renamed or removed here"), and it breaks the rule the L1 rework set: never write the served or localized menu. It is one ordinary click on HotCRM, the card's acceptance app, whose 销售 group ends with contributed entries. The same fallback also writes a served copy when the mount-time stored read failed (then no entry is treated as contributed and its controls are open), and when an entry the editor moved has left the stored menu in the meantime (probe: the entry comes back with its zh-CN label). No test covers a move next to a contributed entry; the one contributed-entry test only checks that its own controls are disabled. Fix: in `rebaseMenuEdits`, never write the served copy of an entry that `served` holds and `stored` does not (skip it; only an entry absent from `served` is an addition), keep such entries out of the order comparison in `staysInOrder`, and stop 「Move up」, 「Move down」 and a drop from crossing a contributed entry. Add a save-level test: a move beside a contributed entry writes no contributed entry.

S2 (should-fix): A new entry's id is minted against the served menu, not the stored one. `newEntryId(menu)` and `withEntryIds(served)` take the first free `nav_item_N` in what the reader was shown. A stored entry the reader was not shown (pruned by `filterNav`, or an empty group) can already hold that id. Then the save matches the two by id. Probe: stored `[lead, nav_item_1(hidden)]`, the reader adds an object and it gets `nav_item_1`; the menu written is the stored one unchanged, so the add is dropped while the bar reports a save. In the id-less variant the edit lands on the wrong entry. Probe: stored `[lead (no id), nav_item_1(hidden)]`, the shown `lead` is given `nav_item_1`, the reader removes it; the menu written is `[lead]`, so the hidden entry is removed for everyone and the one the reader removed stays. `nav_item_N` ids are what this editor itself writes, so they will be common. Fix: mint or re-mint added ids against the stored menu at save time, and give id-less served entries ids that cannot collide with a stored id.

N5 (nit): A link added in a language other than the default stores the typed label as the entry's base label for every language. The ruling covers renames, so this is outside its letter, but the reason behind it applies. It fits #36504.

N6 (nit): Nothing pins the stored version between the layered read and the draft write. A publish by someone else that lands in that short window is overwritten by this save. The first-write pin only refuses a pending draft.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/36363-design-mode-menu-editing.md` still takes `patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present and line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset.

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. The delta adds three published `@object-ui/i18n` keys per locale and removes or narrows nothing a consumer reads. The rename field closing in a non-default language narrows only a control this same PR introduces, which no release has shipped.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The save writes only keys the spec already accepts on `navigation` entries and the existing `overrides` body. It adds no authorable key, value or type.
- Level. `patch` on both packages is right for a non-protocol change (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3).
- Changeset text. One sentence is not true of the tree: "An entry another package puts into the menu ... is not moved, renamed or removed here." M1 shows a path that moves and stores it. The text becomes true once M1 is fixed; it needs no rewording then.

### ③ Boundary flags

- L1 REWORK 7081226692 items 1 and 2 (translated labels, pruned entries). Answered in the tree for the app's own entries, with the two tests asked for. Not fully answered for contributed entries (M1).
- L1 item 3 (live acceptance on HotCRM in zh-CN). The PR body records the run and its requests. A body claim is not a tree fact and no check-run covers it; it stays the L1 seat's and the coordinator's check. The moves in that run were not next to a contributed entry.
- L1 item 4 and seat ruling (4). The tree follows the ruling. The ruling itself is not posted on the card or the PR; it is stated only in the PR body and in #36504. The seat should post it where the record of this card can cite it.
- Default language taken as the source language. Declared in the PR body, with the gap (`i18n.sourceLocale` is not exposed) carried by #36504. Acceptable for this stage.
- ADR-0146 D5, the entry move under #36485, the two-choice leave prompt, apps split in areas, and the card's unverified items: unchanged since the earlier record, and answered there.
- `open_questions`: the PR declares none beyond the above.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5). Not applicable. The delta adds one metadata read (the layered read of one app) and one read of the locale list. It adds no data query, no id materialisation and no in-app join over records.
- Out of scope: #36366 and #36504 were not reviewed.
